title: Pollutions sensorielles
bookshelves: Category: Earth Sciences, Geography, Environment, Planning
Category: Technology, Engineering, Agriculture, Industrial processes
summary: Organisms interact with one another and with their environment through their senses. However, human infrastructure and activities emit artificial light at night, as well as noise and volatile molecules that can degrade and fragment sensory landscapes, making ecosystems less functional. While the artificialization of natural environments is identified as one of the primary causes of biodiversity loss, these forms of sensory pollution remain a minor concern in public policy. This book first re-establishes sensory perception as central to the functioning of ecosystems and landscapes. It then examines the impact of light, noise, and odor pollution on wildlife and ecosystems, before proposing solutions to mitigate them. Finally, it calls for greater consideration of these issues in land-use planning through ecological network policies.
